correctness.rationale: All n≥3,t>0 and all individually nonnegative edge weights under an exact one-unit priced budget are covered. Averaging Rayleigh quotients on the two (n−1)-dimensional orthogonal zero-sum modes yields valid trace upper bounds for arbitrary nonsymmetric weights. Their lower envelope is maximized at the stated total matching weight (or critical interval). The displayed four-summand full spectrum for orbit-constant rates attains the upper bound. Saturation of the antisymmetric trace bound forces the entire antisymmetric zero-sum space into the λ2 eigenspace; its two block equations force all offmatching rates equal by connectedness of the index incidence graph for n≥3 and then all matching rates equal. This proves complete optimizer classification and uniqueness off the threshold. The exact-rational checker tested 693 eigenvector equations, 126 projector identities, 1260 feasible-allocation inequalities, and 28 critical spectra. These finite checks supplement rather than establish universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The named general convex semidefinite treatment [Sun et al., DOI 10.1137/S0036144504443821] provides an optimization framework and dual, but inspected sections and examples do not formulate this two-price matching optimum or classify the entire nonsymmetric optimal set. Symmetry study [Boyd et al., DOI 10.1137/070689413] concerns discrete-time second-largest-eigenvalue-modulus minimization, even where it treats complete bipartite graphs. A published crown-graph Laplacian spectrum [DOI 10.21831/pythagoras.v19i1.60818] is the unweighted deleted-matching boundary, not a price-parametric optimization. The four projector-based equality and uniqueness conclusions are not directly implied by these references. Semantic searches and the published research registry found no explicit exact equivalent; this does not prove absolute historical novelty.

value.rationale: A fixed priced perfect matching in balanced complete bipartite networks models retaining or replacing paired cross-class links under a common rate budget. The work resolves the natural decision exactly for arbitrary network size, with an all-allocations theorem rather than only orbit-optimal rates. The first-order conductance jump at a strictly finite premium, continuous spectral gap, critical full face and eigenvalue multiplicity transition reveal non-obvious structure; neither a simple fixed-weight spectrum nor a cosmetic SDP substitution establishes those properties. The result yields explicit designs without solving a numerical SDP.
